title: Quasi-coherent algebra direct image and smooth-chart comparison
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ be algebraic stacks over $k$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]. Use quasi-coherent algebras, surjections and global sections from [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Tensor pullback of quasi-coherent commutative algebras has a right adjoint $f_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}$ with values in quasi-coherent commutative algebras. On every smooth scheme test $t:T\to\mathcal Y$, its restriction to the smooth-etale site has the functorial algebra identification $$ (f_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A)(T)=\Gamma(\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T,\mathcal A|_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}T}). $$ Thus this restriction is the direct image on that site. Smooth and etale have the chart meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-etale-morphism]. For any further quasi-compact quasi-separated $g:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ to an algebraic stack over $k$, there is a canonical natural algebra isomorphism $g_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}f_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A\simeq(g\circ f)_{\mathrm{QCoh},*}\mathcal A$, compatible with algebra homomorphisms. For quasi-coherent algebras on any algebraic stack over $k$, a morphism is a surjection in the fppf-sheaf sense if and only if its restriction to the smooth-etale site is a surjection of sheaves; equivalently every section on a smooth scheme test has a lift after an etale covering of that test. This does not assert that naive direct image on the entire big fppf site is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tags 077A (proposition-direct-image-quasi-coherent), 0GQQ (lemma-direct-image-quasi-coherent-over-flat), 0GQR (remark-direct-image-quasi-coherent-tensor), 0GQF (lemma-quasi-coherent-check-exact). The algebra adjunction and composition are the multiplicative form of the right adjunction; smooth tests are flat. No claim about naive big-fppf quasi-coherence is made.

proof.text: Put $P=f^*$ and $R=R_f$ using the module adjunction [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-module-adjunction], with counit $\epsilon:PR\to\mathrm{id}$. By [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness], $B=R\mathcal A$, $B\otimes B$ and all tensor powers are quasi-coherent. Pullback is tensor-compatible by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]; [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction] identifies the stack pullback with the ringed-site pullback and identifies $P\mathcal O_{\mathcal Y}$ with $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$. Define $m_B:B\otimes B\to B$ as the module transpose of $m_{\mathcal A}\circ(\epsilon_{\mathcal A}\otimes\epsilon_{\mathcal A})$, and $u_B:\mathcal O_{\mathcal Y}\to B$ as the transpose of $u_{\mathcal A}:\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal A$. Thus the underlying module and both algebra operations are actual constructions from the stated adjunction.

Check the algebra laws by the injectivity of the module adjunction bijections. The transposes of $m_B(m_B\otimes1)$ and $m_B(1\otimes m_B)$ are respectively $m_{\mathcal A}(m_{\mathcal A}\otimes1)\epsilon_{\mathcal A}^{\otimes3}$ and $m_{\mathcal A}(1\otimes m_{\mathcal A})\epsilon_{\mathcal A}^{\otimes3}$; they agree by associativity of $\mathcal A$. For commutativity the two transposes are $m_{\mathcal A}\epsilon^{\otimes2}$ and $m_{\mathcal A}\tau\epsilon^{\otimes2}$, equal by commutativity of $\mathcal A$. For each unit law the transpose is $m_{\mathcal A}(u_{\mathcal A}\otimes1)\epsilon$ or $m_{\mathcal A}(1\otimes u_{\mathcal A})\epsilon$, respectively, hence is $\epsilon$, the transpose of $1_B$. Here the tensor identifications are the canonical section-tensor identifications, so the displayed substitutions also include the associators and unitors. For an algebra map $v:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\prime$, naturality $\epsilon_{\mathcal A\prime}PRv=v\epsilon_{\mathcal A}$ proves after the same transposition that $Rv$ preserves $m$ and $u$. Thus these assignments form a functor on commutative algebras.

source.place: 077A and 0GQR: direct verification of the multiplication, unit and functor laws

proof.text: For a quasi-coherent algebra $C$ on $\mathcal Y$, the transpose of a module map $h:C\to R\mathcal A$ is $\bar h=\epsilon_{\mathcal A}Ph$. Transposing the equality $h m_C=m_B(h\otimes h)$ gives exactly $\bar h\,P(m_C)=m_{\mathcal A}(\bar h\otimes\bar h)$, and transposing $h u_C=u_B$ gives exactly $\bar h\,P(u_C)=u_{\mathcal A}$. Consequently $h$ is an algebra homomorphism if and only if $\bar h$ is. Restricting the natural module bijections to these subsets proves the required algebra adjunction, with tensor pullback as left adjoint.

source.place: 077A: restriction of the module adjunction to multiplication-preserving and unit-preserving maps

proof.text: Let $t:T\to\mathcal Y$ be a smooth scheme test. Smooth scheme charts are flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], so $t$ is a flat test. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-flat-module-pushforward-comparison] to the underlying module of $\mathcal A$. Its comparison is the displayed section identification in the statement. That node identifies the tensor pairing and the unit with the ordinary section tensor and regular-function maps. Composing the tensor pairing with $R(m_{\mathcal A})$ gives precisely $m_B$ by its defining transpose. Hence the comparison preserves multiplication and the unit, and is an algebra isomorphism. Its naturality supplies compatibility with algebra maps and all arrows between smooth tests. Restricting further to etale coverings is exactly the section definition of direct image on the smooth-etale site; the fibre stacks are algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products].

For $g:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal Z$ as in the statement, [lem-sfb-stack-qcqs-composition-affine] ensures that $gf$ is qcqs. The preceding construction applies to $f,g,gf$. By [lem-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-scheme-restriction], pullback of quasi-coherent algebras is precomposition, so $(gf)^*=f^*g^*$ with the canonical identifications (the value at a test $x$ is the value at $g(f(x))$). Apply [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] in the categories of quasi-coherent commutative algebras to obtain $R_gR_f\simeq R_{gf}$, the inverse of its displayed orientation if necessary. Because the comparison is formed in these algebra categories, every component is an algebra homomorphism and naturality is exactly compatibility with algebra homomorphisms. Its pasted counit also fixes the canonical choice.

source.place: 077A: uniqueness of right adjoints applied to the algebra adjunction; Stacks stacks-morphisms.tex Tags 050W and 050K for qcqs composition

proof.text: For an algebra map $u:A\to B$ on an arbitrary algebraic stack, first forget only multiplication. By [lem-sfb-stack-qcoh-flat-atlas-exactness], the cokernel in quasi-coherent modules is its cokernel in fppf module sheaves; thus $u$ is an epimorphism of quasi-coherent modules if and only if it is fppf-locally surjective. Every smooth scheme test is flat by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The same module lemma says that epimorphisms restrict to surjections on each test's small etale site, which is the stated local etale lifting condition. Conversely, if every smooth test has that lifting condition, choose the smooth surjective atlas supplied by [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. On this flat atlas the restriction is surjective, and the module lemma detects that $u$ is an epimorphism of quasi-coherent modules. Its ambient fppf cokernel is therefore zero, so it is fppf-locally surjective. All lifting statements concern underlying sets of sections of the same algebra map; forgetting multiplication changes none of them. This proves both directions without requiring direct image to preserve surjections.
